title: 100BASE-TX Ethernet Control Node
description: The split between what BRIEF.md fixes and what it leaves open. Every fixed_requirements entry carries the verbatim brief text that substantiates it, bound to the recorded brief digest. An open_decisions entry is a choice for the design agent: record it in 'chosen' with 'rationale', and never move it into fixed_requirements. Missing details are design freedom, not permission to fabricate unstated user requirements.

brief.authority: supplied by the benchmark; authoritative; preserved byte for byte and never edited

derivation.method: BRIEF.md was read and split; no design decision was taken. Every fixed_requirements entry, and every spec-table row sourced from the brief, carries a quotation that was checked by literal substring match against the brief bytes digested above. The build refuses to emit this file if any quotation is not found.
derivation.review: two rounds of adversarial review against the brief, looking for invented requirements, lost requirements, evidence supporting a weaker claim than the one made beside it, and worksheet questions that presuppose their own answer

fixed_requirements.requirement: The board is a 100BASE-TX Ethernet control board.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: Create a 100BASE-TX Ethernet control board using an MCU with RMII and an external PHY.

fixed_requirements.requirement: The design uses an MCU that provides an RMII interface.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: using an MCU with RMII and an external PHY. Provide an RJ45

fixed_requirements.requirement: The Ethernet PHY is external to the MCU (an integrated-PHY MCU does not satisfy the brief).
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: an MCU with RMII and an external PHY. Provide an RJ45 with integrated magnetics if convenient

fixed_requirements.requirement: An RJ45 is provided; magnetics integrated into it are asked for on the stated condition 'if convenient', so integration is conditional, not mandated, and the scaffold takes no position on which way it should go.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: Provide an RJ45 with integrated magnetics if convenient, link/activity LEDs

fixed_requirements.requirement: Link and activity LEDs are provided.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: if convenient, link/activity LEDs, USB-C for service power/debug

fixed_requirements.requirement: A USB-C port is provided, serving service power and debug.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: link/activity LEDs, USB-C for service power/debug, and a small expansion header.

fixed_requirements.requirement: A small expansion header is provided.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: USB-C for service power/debug, and a small expansion header.

fixed_requirements.requirement: The RMII reference clock is a 50 MHz architecture, and the specific architecture must be the one recommended by the devices actually selected.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: Use a 50 MHz RMII reference-clock architecture recommended by the selected devices.

fixed_requirements.requirement: The Ethernet pairs are routed as controlled differential pairs over the whole run from PHY to magnetics.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: Route Ethernet pairs as controlled differential pairs from PHY to magnetics

fixed_requirements.requirement: The PHY analog supplies are kept quiet.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: from PHY to magnetics, keep PHY analog supplies quiet, and maintain continuous reference planes

fixed_requirements.requirement: Reference planes are continuous beneath RMII and other high-speed signals.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: maintain continuous reference planes under RMII/high-speed signals.
under RMII/high-speed signals. Four layers required.

fixed_requirements.requirement: Stated brief requirements are authoritative; open choices must be made and documented as engineering decisions, not converted into invented user requirements.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: Treat stated requirements as authoritative; where the brief leaves choices open, make and document reasonable engineering decisions rather than inventing hidden user requirements.

fixed_requirements.requirement: This repository stays a consumer of the shared PCBA_AutoDesignAndTest toolkit; board-specific logic must not accumulate inside the toolkit.
fixed_requirements.brief_evidence: The repository should remain a consumer of the shared `PCBA_AutoDesignAndTest` toolkit rather than accumulating board-specific logic in the toolkit.

open_decisions.decision: Which MCU is used — family, core, package, memory, peripheral set, and how much headroom the control application needs.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief asks only for 'an MCU with RMII'. No vendor, family, package, or resource figure appears anywhere in the brief or metadata.

open_decisions.decision: Which external Ethernet PHY is used, and in what package and supply configuration.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief names only 'an external PHY'. Every downstream constraint the brief imposes (clock architecture, analog supply quieting, MDIO/strapping) depends on this choice, which the brief leaves entirely to the design agent.

open_decisions.decision: The 50 MHz RMII reference-clock topology: which device sources the clock, whether a discrete oscillator is used, and how the clock is distributed to the devices that need it and terminated.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief fixes 50 MHz and fixes that the architecture be 'recommended by the selected devices' — which means the topology is undetermined until OPEN-01 and OPEN-02 are resolved and their datasheets are read.

open_decisions.decision: Integrated-magnetics RJ45 versus a plain RJ45 with discrete magnetics, and the associated isolation/creepage handling.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief hedges with 'if convenient', explicitly declining to mandate integration. It gives no part number, no isolation rating, and no availability constraint to decide it on.

open_decisions.decision: The magnetics-side network: centre-tap treatment, the line-side termination network and its topology, and how the RJ45 shield and any chassis ground relate to signal ground.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief mentions magnetics only as a routing endpoint. It is silent on termination topology, shield bonding, and chassis-ground strategy, so the network follows from the magnetics datasheet and the designer's reasoning, not from this scaffold.

open_decisions.decision: Link/activity LED count, colours, placement (in-connector versus board-mounted), and whether they are driven by the PHY, the MCU, or link hardware.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief states only 'link/activity LEDs'. It fixes neither quantity, colour, drive polarity, nor which device drives them.

open_decisions.decision: The USB-C port's electrical role: what power role the port takes, how that role is configured at the connector, what current budget it is designed to, and whether the connector also carries a USB data interface or only debug signalling.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief says 'USB-C for service power/debug' and stops there — no power role, no power level, no data role, and no negotiation or configuration method is stated.

open_decisions.decision: How the MCU is programmed and debugged — the physical debug interface, and whether it is exposed on the USB-C port, on the expansion header, on test pads, or on a dedicated connector.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief attaches 'debug' to the USB-C port but never names a programming or debug interface, so the mechanism is unfixed.

open_decisions.decision: Expansion header pinout, signal set, pin count, pitch, gender, and location.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief asks for 'a small expansion header' with no signal list, no pin count, no pitch, and no definition of 'small'.

open_decisions.decision: Power architecture: what supplies the board in normal operation besides USB-C service power, the rail voltages, the regulator topologies, and how the PHY analog rail is separated from digital rails.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief imposes an outcome ('keep PHY analog supplies quiet') but names no rail, no regulator type, no filtering method, and no primary power input other than USB-C service power.

open_decisions.decision: The four-layer stackup: layer ordering and roles, dielectric thicknesses, copper weights, and which layers carry the continuous reference planes the brief requires.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief fixes the layer count at four and requires plane continuity, but states nothing about stackup ordering, materials, or thicknesses.

open_decisions.decision: The differential impedance target for the Ethernet pairs and the single-ended impedance treatment (if any) for RMII, plus the trace geometry that realises them in the chosen stackup.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief requires 'controlled differential pairs' but states no impedance value, tolerance, or geometry — those follow from the stackup and the PHY's requirements, neither of which is fixed.

open_decisions.decision: The RMII timing/skew budget: allowed trace-length mismatch, total lengths, and layer-change and return-path policy for RMII clock and data.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief lists RMII clock/data as a stressor and requires continuous reference planes, but gives no length, skew, or timing number and prescribes no layer-change or stitching technique; these must come from the selected devices' datasheets and the designer's own reasoning.

open_decisions.decision: Protection strategy for the Ethernet port, the USB-C port, and the expansion header — whether protection is added at all, and if so ESD, surge, and common-mode suppression, including whether any added device's capacitance is compatible with 100BASE-TX pairs.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief is silent on protection entirely. It names no environment, no ESD level, and no standard to design against.

open_decisions.decision: Board outline, dimensions, mounting-hole pattern, keepouts, connector edge placement, and any enclosure interface.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief states no mechanical constraint of any kind — no size, no shape, no mounting, no enclosure.

open_decisions.decision: PHY configuration provisioning: PHY address and mode strapping, MDIO access, reset sequencing between MCU and PHY, and any MAC-address storage.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief does not mention strapping, MDIO, reset order, or MAC-address provisioning at all, though a working PHY link requires decisions on each.

open_decisions.decision: Manufacturing targets: fabricator and process class, minimum trace/space and via geometry, surface finish, assembly side(s), and component sourcing/lifecycle criteria.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief names no vendor, process, finish, or sourcing constraint; only the four-layer count is fixed.

open_decisions.decision: Bring-up and test provisions: test points, link-verification method, and what evidence will be produced to show the impedance, plane-continuity, and clock requirements were actually met.
open_decisions.why_open: The brief states design constraints but prescribes no verification method or acceptance evidence for them.
